title: Vera Rubin hardware reference database
basis: internal docs + local source + our measurements (private hwdb; numbers not reproduced here)
gap_analysis: v1 of the private hwdb is live: INDEX with ten key facts, 11 topic files (block-scaled MMA 2x-K forms and rates, TMEM exclusive allocation, oversized shared memory, clusters, TMA incl. counted stores and gather4, launch/PDL/CLC costs, SM resources and FP32 rate, HBM/L2/locality domains, NVLink6/multimem, build arch and CuTe DSL support, worked examples) and 13 workstream briefs with features, design hints and the hardware limit at each deployed shape. Key new confirmations: mixed MXFP8 x MXFP4 MMA runs at the FP8 rate (only FP4 x FP4 gets the FP4 rate); the 2x-K form is selected by instruction-descriptor bits on sm_107a only; counted TMA stores signal completion at the destination; CLC is supported but static scheduling wins for small decode work. Model observations for owners: decode expert rows already assume die-local HBM, dense decode rows the default rate (die-localizing dense weights can beat model achievable); the prefill indexer-score row is costed at roughly the sm_100-form FP8 rate, below what a native kernel can reach.
inefficiencies: Hardware probes (FFMA/FFMA2 rate, oversized shared memory launch + occupancy, graph/PDL per-kernel cost, die-local bandwidth, legacy HMMA, MUFU, shared atomics, L2 residency across kernels, cross-die L2 caching) are queued on the Rhea pool; no free GPU yet
Some Rubin ISA features (counted TMA stores, early A-buffer release, descriptor circular buffers, TMA L2 management) have no confirmed PTX/CuTe DSL spelling yet
